title: Viscoelastic rod under suddenly applied constant axial traction
purpose: Verify the three-dimensional global generalized-Maxwell procedure against the public Abaqus/Standard viscoelastic rod benchmark and its analytical creep-compliance solution.
physics: Three-dimensional small-strain isotropic linear viscoelastic creep under prescribed traction

reference.title: Abaqus Benchmarks Guide: Viscoelastic rod subjected to constant axial load
reference.underlying_reference: Collingwood, Becker and Miller (1985); analytical inversion follows Pipkin (1972).

execution.evidence: A 254 mm three-dimensional brick rod uses the published shear Prony conversion, constant bulk modulus, symmetry constraints and 0.689 MPa end traction. A declared nonuniform physical-time grid resolves the 0.001 s loading ramp and the 50 s creep hold.

observables: Volume-averaged axial strain after the 0.001 s loading ramp.
Volume-averaged axial strain after the 50 s constant-traction hold.
Effective Poisson ratio from volume-averaged lateral and axial strain.
Difference from the published continuous creep-compliance curve.
acceptance: The 0.001 s and 50 s axial strains must match the published Abaqus values within their explicit Golden tolerances.
The 50 s effective Poisson ratio must match the published Abaqus value.
The 50 s strain must also remain within 0.2% of the continuous analytical creep-compliance curve.
The public model.step API must accept and identify the nonuniform physical-time grid.

quantities.name: axial_strain_at_0.001_seconds
quantities.description: Published Abaqus result after the 0.001 s near-instantaneous loading step.

quantities.name: axial_strain_at_50_seconds
quantities.description: Published Abaqus result after the 50 s constant-traction creep hold.

quantities.name: effective_poisson_ratio_at_50_seconds
quantities.description: Published long-time effective Poisson ratio extracted from lateral and axial strain.

limitations: This verifies small-strain quasi-static viscoelasticity, not the separate large-strain Abaqus variant.
The AgentFEM model uses a compact three-dimensional hexahedral realization instead of the reference axisymmetric hybrid element.
Distributed portable restart remains a separate advancement gate; this external benchmark retains the published nonuniform time grid rather than replacing it with adaptive control.
